dedupe_keys.name: cims critical infrastructure modeling system idaho national laboratory

description: CIMS, the Critical Infrastructure Modeling System, is a three-dimensional modelling and simulation environment for analysing dependencies within one infrastructure and interdependencies between several. Infrastructure components and their links are placed in a 3D scene, and a discrete event simulation engine propagates perturbations so that users can see, through visual cues and text displays, how outages spread, for example areas that lose power, denial of service or access, and disrupted operations, and so identify emergent patterns of cascading consequences. It was developed at Idaho National Laboratory by Donald Dudenhoeffer, May Permann, Steven Woolsey and James Forsmann, registered as software in October 2004 and described at the 2006 Winter Simulation Conference. The DOE code record lists it as closed source, so it is not publicly downloadable and access would be through INL. Caveats: it is legacy software, models are built by hand for each area, and the link logic is qualitative, not physics-based. It is a reference design for cascading failure and situational awareness tools in interdependent infrastructure simulation; a related record is the Netherlands socio-technical infrastructure interdependencies dataset.
name: CIMS Critical Infrastructure Modeling System (Idaho National Laboratory)
notes: The Netherlands interdependencies dataset is on the integrator branch and is named in prose only; the agent_based kind reflects the component-level discrete event logic described in the WSC paper abstract.
